title: Hydraulic Power Available

H.description: Head (gross or net depending on context)

applicability: Fundamental power equation. P(kW) = 9.81 × Q × H. Quick estimate: ~10 kW per m³/s per m of head. Use H_net for power at turbine; H_gross for total potential.

title: Generator Output Power
equation: P_gen = ρ × g × Q × H_net × η_t × η_g

P_gen.description: Electrical power output at generator terminals

applicability: P_gen(kW) = 9.81 × Q × H_net × η_t × η_g. Net head deductions: penstock friction, trashrack, intake, bends, valves (typically 3–10% of gross head). Transformer losses and auxiliary power reduce further to net plant output.

title: Specific Speed (Turbine)
applicability: Ns(US) ranges: Pelton 4–60, Francis 60–400, Kaplan/propeller 300–900+. Metric form: ns = N√P(kW)/H(m)^1.25 where ns ≈ Ns/4.45. Determines optimal turbine type and geometry.

title: Annual Energy Production
applicability: Capacity factor depends on hydrology and plant type. Run-of-river: 0.30–0.50. Storage: 0.25–0.55 (lower CF because used for peaking). More precise: E = Σ(P_i × Δt_i) using flow duration curve with efficiency at each flow.

title: Synchronous Speed (Generator)

f.description: Grid frequency (60 Hz in Americas, 50 Hz elsewhere)

applicability: Generator must rotate at synchronous speed to produce correct frequency. Turbine speed must match (or be geared to) synchronous speed. More poles → lower speed → larger, more expensive generator but better suited to low-head turbines.

title: Thoma Cavitation Coefficient (Turbine Setting)

H_s.description: Turbine setting height above tailwater (positive = above)

applicability: Requirement: σ_plant ≥ σ_critical (from model test, typically 0.01–0.10 for Francis, 0.2–0.8 for Kaplan). Determines maximum elevation of turbine runner above tailwater. At altitude, reduced P_atm requires lower turbine setting. Francis turbines at high head often set below tailwater.

title: Pelton Jet Velocity and Bucket Speed

U_optimal.description: Optimal bucket peripheral speed for maximum efficiency

applicability: At U/V_jet = 0.5, maximum energy transfer occurs (all kinetic energy extracted from jet in the runner reference frame). Runner diameter: D = 60 × U / (π × N). Jet diameter: d_jet = √(4Q/(n_jets × π × V_jet)).

title: Economic Penstock Diameter
applicability: Very approximate. True economic diameter from life-cycle cost analysis: minimize (annual capital cost of steel + annual energy loss). Rule of thumb: head loss in penstock ≤ 4–8% of gross head. Higher energy values → larger economic diameter.

title: Pumped Storage Round-Trip Efficiency
equation: η_RT = η_pump × η_motor × η_turbine × η_generator × (1 - f_loss)
applicability: Typical round-trip: 70–85%. Modern variable-speed units: 78–82%. Pumped storage is economically justified by time-of-use electricity price differential.

title: Flow Duration — Power at Exceedance Percentile

P_x.description: Power available at exceedance percentile x%

Q_x.description: Flow equalled or exceeded x% of the time (from flow duration curve)

H_net.description: Net head at Q_x (may vary with tailwater)

η_overall.description: Overall efficiency at Q_x (varies with flow)

applicability: Key percentiles: Q30 for installed capacity (firm power design), Q90–Q95 for firm energy (minimum reliable flow). Energy = integral of power curve over 8760 hours. Discretize flow duration into intervals and sum.
